name: Upma
subtitle: soft savoury semolina with crackling dal, ginger and curry leaves

ingredients.note: coarse bombay rava, not the fine idli variety

prepNotes: Dry-roast the rava on low heat for 4 minutes until it smells toasty and moves loosely in the pan, then tip it out.
Boil the water and keep it on a low flame. It must go in hot or the upma turns lumpy.
Have everything chopped before you start; the tempering to the finish takes six minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds until they jump and quieten.
Add the urad dal and chana dal and fry until both turn a light red-gold, about 90 seconds.
steps.tip: The dals are what give upma its crunch; pale dal means no texture.

steps.text: Add the cashews, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves and fry 30 seconds until the leaves crisp.
Add the onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 4 minutes, no browning.
Pour in the boiling water with the salt and let it come back to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and add the roasted rava in a thin steady stream with one hand while stirring hard with the other.
steps.tip: Dumping it in all at once is exactly how you get lumps.

steps.text: Keep stirring for 2 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Cover and steam on the lowest heat for 3 minutes, then turn off and rest 2 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, squeeze over the lemon and scatter the coriander.

storage: Best within a few hours. Refrigerate up to 2 days and revive by steaming with 2 tbsp water sprinkled over; microwaving dries it out.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
